newsitem.title: USA: Argentina's Menem will fight corruption-Cavallo.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem will fight corruption-Cavallo.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem will stand by a pledge to fight corruption, former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said on Wednesday.

Cavallo, who created a political uproar Tuesday by charging two cabinet members with manipulating judges, questioned published reports that Menem denied the existance of "mafias" within the government.

"I don't believe that President Menem said that my statements were lies because last week he promised to place himself at the front of the fight against corruption," Cavallo said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Cavallo, who was fired in July after a series of highly publicized squabbles, said he had met with Menem after watching the president declare a campaign against corruption.
"I visited him to congratulate him for having decided to lead this fight," Cavallo said. "I see him as very committed to it ... I think he will do his best to lead this fight agains the mafias."
Reuters reported earlier Wednesday that the Argentine president dismissed as lies Cavallo's charges against Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan.
"Of course that's a lie," Menem told foreign correspondents about Cavallo's charges. "There are no mafias in the government."
In the RFTV interview, Cavallo declined to elaborate on his allegations against the two cabinet ministers.
He did say that Menem had told him one year ago that Cavallo was right to root out corruption but that the battle would need to be waged at an "appropriate time."
"Some people think that President Menem is not sincere, but I still beleive in him," Cavallo said. "He is a person who chooses the right timing for everything."

On Tuesday Cavallo had said that Corach tried to remove a judge from investigating a gold-export fraud case and replace him with another magistrate "who had failed to find any crime commited by gold exporters."

Cavallo also said that Corach once wrote on a paper napkin the name of several judges and state prosecutors and bragged, "These do as I say." Jassan used to call judges and prosecutors to give them instructions on issues he was interested in, Cavallo said.

Corach rejected the charges on Tuesday. In a statement, he called them "totally irresponsible and reflecting (Cavallo's) state of emotional imbalance." He also said he had issued instructions for immediate judicial action.
A spokesman for Jassan said the justice minister had no immediate plans to react to Cavallo's charges.
Local Argentine bonds fell on the concerns over the political consequences of the charges, but Cavallo said his comments should not affect international investment.
"It should not increase the assesment of country risk," Cavallo told RFTV. "When you have an open discussion of local judicariary and security problems there are better prospects for a solution."
